name: Equal Product
description: You are given four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$. Let's name a tuple $$$(x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2)$$$ as good if: $$$1 \le x_1 \lt x_2 \le n$$$; $$$1 \le y_2 \lt y_1 \le m$$$; $$$x_1 \cdot y_1 = x_2 \cdot y_2$$$; $$$l \le x_1 \cdot y_1 \le r$$$. Find any good tuple for each $$$x_1$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ inclusive .
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ ($$$1 \le l \le r \le nm$$$).
output_specification: For each $$$x_1$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ inclusive: if there are no such four integers, print $$$-1$$$; otherwise, print four integers $$$x_1$$$, $$$y_1$$$, $$$x_2$$$ and $$$y_2$$$. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.
